argument: Ran the pair and tape checks from my seat. Ratio data confirmed (EEM/ACWI 0.4066, 50th pct, z +0.14, as of Aug 7), but the absolute momentum picture undercuts the timing: EEM is +36.4% 1y, +12.7% 6m, and just bounced +2.4% on the week / +0.95% on the last session (data_platform, Aug 7 close). The proposal shorts relative value into a strong absolute uptrend, at mid-range, after the ratio has already moved -6.1% over 3m — the entry is chasing, and the 0.4245 stop sits ~4.4% away against a pair that just rallied 2.4% in five sessions. One Hormuz de-escalation headline and the stop is in play before the sanctions catalyst (Aug 31, date TBD) even arrives. Second, an internal inconsistency: driver #3 is AI/semis derating, but ACWI is ~65% US and carries the same mega-cap AI complex in heavier cap-weighted concentration than EEM's TSMC/Samsung/Tencent stack. If the AI complex is the source of underperformance, this pair is a muddy expression of it — a genuine AI derating could compress ACWI's US leg as much as EEM's tech leg, neutralizing the trade exactly when the thesis is 'working.' Third, from the consumer side of my mandate: the energy terms-of-trade tax on China/India/CEE consumers is real but five months old, and EM consumer-facing demand has absorbed it so far — you don't get +36% 1y in an importer-heavy index if the consumer transmission is biting. My own driver board has China consumer recovery as a live swing factor for NKE/luxury/travel; this short is implicitly short that recovery without any consumer-level evidence (comp trends, card data, retail sales) cited in the proposal. The bear case (de-escalation, crude <$70) at 25% probability looks underpriced given how fast a crowded-consensus-long market squeezes when the shock premium unwinds — and de-escalation is a double tailwind for EM importers (ToT relief + FX). Net: direction is defensible, entry and instrument are not. Conviction 6 reads a touch high; I'd want 5, or a better entry closer to 0.42 with the Graham act vote as a confirmed catalyst date rather than TBD.
